aspects.says: charAt and substring throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException outside the string, the end index of substring is exclusive, and every method throws NullPointerException on null.
aspects.reason: lookup facts listed in the reference table; the segment practice relies on the exclusive end index without grading it on its own, and a wrong bound fails at once with an exception the reader sees

aspects.says: length(), charAt() and substring() count UTF-16 units, so a character outside the BMP takes two and a cut at a unit index can split it.
basis: section:length(), charAt() and substring() Count UTF-16 Units, So an Emoji Counts Twice

aspects.says: length() of a text made of emoji is twice the number of characters the user sees.
basis: section:length(), charAt() and substring() Count UTF-16 Units, So an Emoji Counts Twice

aspects.says: replace() replaces every occurrence of literal text, while replaceAll() reads its first argument as a regex and its replacement's $ and \ as syntax.
basis: section:replace() Replaces Every Literal Match; replaceAll() Interprets Both of Its Arguments

aspects.says: split(regex) removes trailing empty strings and keeps the others; a negative limit keeps every field.
basis: section:split() Takes a Regex and Drops Trailing Empty Strings

aspects.says: split() reads its argument as a regular expression, so a delimiter such as | or . must be quoted.
basis: section:split() Takes a Regex and Drops Trailing Empty Strings

aspects.says: In Java 21 substring copies the characters it returns, so a short piece of a long line doesn't keep the line in memory.
basis: section:length(), charAt() and substring() Count UTF-16 Units, So an Emoji Counts Twice

aspects.says: trim() removes only characters up to U+0020, strip() and isBlank() use Character.isWhitespace, and neither removes the no-break space U+00A0.
basis: section:trim() Stops at U+0020, strip() at Unicode Whitespace, and Neither Removes a No-Break Space
